title: The content of the view: Gram form, invisible data and well-defined companion invariants

key_results.statement: For an admissible joint state, the view of $A$ is the Gram matrix of the branch vectors $\lvert\psi_h\rangle=(\langle h\rvert\otimes\mathbb 1_{\bar A})\lvert\Psi\rangle$: $(V_A)_{hh'}=\langle\psi_{h'}\vert\psi_h\rangle$, and $p_h=\lVert\psi_h\rVert^2$.

For every decomposition $\lvert\Psi\rangle=\sum_ha_h\lvert h\rangle\otimes\lvert E_h\rangle$ of the form (1.6), $\lvert\psi_h\rangle=a_h\lvert E_h\rangle$ for every joint place $h$ of $A$; inserted in (2.2) this gives (1.7), $(V_A)_{hh'}=a_ha_{h'}^{*}\langle E_{h'}\vert E_h\rangle$, so (2.2) is the witness rule written without the convention-dependent split.
$V_A$ is a density operator on $\mathcal H_A$: $V_A=V_A^{\dagger}\ge0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}V_A=\sum_hp_h=1$; moreover $\langle h\vert V_A\vert h'\rangle=0$ unless $h,h'\in H_V$.

For every local reading on $A$ whose classes come from a partition $\{S^A_r\}$ of the joint places of $A$, the outcome probability is $p(r)=\sum_{h\in S^A_r}p_h=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\Pi^A_rV_A\bigr)$, with $\Pi^A_r$ the projector onto the span of $S^A_r$.

For admissible states $\lvert\Psi\rangle,\lvert\Phi\rangle$ with branch vectors $\lvert\psi_h\rangle,\lvert\varphi_h\rangle$: $V_A(\Phi)=V_A(\Psi)$ iff there is a unitary $U$ on $\mathcal H_{\bar A}$ with $\lvert\varphi_h\rangle=U\lvert\psi_h\rangle$ for every joint place $h$ of $A$, i.e. $\lvert\Phi\rangle=(\mathbb 1_A\otimes U)\lvert\Psi\rangle$; $U$ is fixed on $\operatorname{span}\{\psi_h\}$ and arbitrary on its orthogonal complement.

Every decomposition (1.6) has $a_h=\sqrt{p_h}\,e^{-i\theta_h}$ and $\lvert E_h\rangle=e^{i\theta_h}\lvert\psi_h\rangle/\sqrt{p_h}$ for $h\in H_V$ with arbitrary real $\theta_h$, and $a_h=0$ for $h\notin H_V$; every such choice is valid, so the convention freedom is exactly the rephasing $\theta_h\to\theta_h+\delta_h$.

$G_{hh'}=\langle E_{h'}\vert E_h\rangle=e^{i(\theta_h-\theta_{h'})}\,(V_A)_{hh'}/\sqrt{p_hp_{h'}}$ for $h,h'\in H_V$; $G$ is Hermitian with $G_{hh}=1$, and a change of convention $\theta\to\theta+\delta$ gives $G_{hh'}\to e^{i(\delta_h-\delta_{h'})}G_{hh'}$.

The cyclic products $W(h_1,\dots,h_k)=G_{h_1h_2}G_{h_2h_3}\cdots G_{h_kh_1}$, $k\ge1$, $h_i\in H_V$, are invariant under every rephasing $G_{hh'}\to e^{i(\theta_h-\theta_{h'})}G_{hh'}$; this holds for every matrix on $H_V$.

$W(h_1,\dots,h_k)=\dfrac{(V_A)_{h_1h_2}(V_A)_{h_2h_3}\cdots(V_A)_{h_kh_1}}{p_{h_1}p_{h_2}\cdots p_{h_k}}$ for $h_i\in H_V$: a function of $V_A$ alone, hence independent of the common phase and of the split (1.6).

Two Gram matrices $G,G'$ of unit vectors on $H_V$ are related by a rephasing, $G'_{hh'}=e^{i(\theta_h-\theta_{h'})}G_{hh'}$ for some real $(\theta_h)$, iff all their cyclic products agree: $W'(h_1,\dots,h_k)=W(h_1,\dots,h_k)$ for all $k\ge1$ and $h_i\in H_V$.
Every well-defined quantity $F$ built from $G$, i.e. invariant under every rephasing, is a function of the cyclic products: $F(G)=f\bigl(\{W(h_1,\dots,h_k)\}_{k\ge1,\ h_i\in H_V}\bigr)$.

For every admissible state $\Psi$ and every permutation $\pi$ of the objects with $T(\pi(a))=T(a)$: $V_{\pi(A)}(\Psi)=J_\pi V_A(\Psi)J_\pi^{\dagger}$, i.e. $\langle h^\pi\vert V_{\pi(A)}\vert h'^\pi\rangle=\langle h\vert V_A\vert h'\rangle$, where $J_\pi:\mathcal H_A\to\mathcal H_{\pi(A)}$ is the natural identification $\lvert h\rangle\mapsto\lvert h^\pi\rangle$.

For a type-preserving permutation $\pi$: $p^{\pi(A)}_{h^\pi}=p^A_h$, $H_V^{\pi(A)}=\{h^\pi:h\in H_V^A\}$ and $W^{\pi(A)}(h_1^\pi,\dots,h_k^\pi)=W^A(h_1,\dots,h_k)$; hence $p_h$ and the cyclic products do not change when the part is replaced by one that differs only in which identical-type instances it contains.

definitions.name: Weight of a joint place of A

open_issues: The weights p_h and the cyclic products W do not determine V_A: they fix it only up to V_A → D V_A D† with D a diagonal unitary in the place basis of A (example: |±⟩⊗|e⟩ with |±⟩ = (|0⟩ ± |1⟩)/√2). The phases lost this way are well-defined data of V_A but not companion data; whether later packages need them is open.

Relation (2.6) does not assert that the state obtained by applying a unitary U on the companion to an admissible state is admissible for every U; which U preserve the admissible subspace depends on the swap condition (1.11) and is out of scope.
Relations (2.15)–(2.16) relate labelled joint places h and h^π; a label-free specification of a part (A7) remains open, and no spatial meaning is attached to p_h, G or W (M1, M4).

consistency_checks.check: Two-branch witness rule: for a|0⟩|E_0⟩ + b|1⟩|E_1⟩ with unit E_0, E_1 the weights are |a|² and |b|² and (V_A)_01 = a·conj(b)·⟨E_1|E_0⟩, the cross term of a|0⟩ + b|1⟩ times the overlap, which vanishes for orthogonal E_0, E_1 as in Section 3 of the base problem.

Product state Ψ = ψ_A ⊗ e with ψ_A = Σ c_h |h⟩: ψ_h = c_h e and (V_A)_hh' = c_h·conj(c_h'), so every cyclic product equals 1, and with θ_h = −arg c_h one gets G_hh' = 1 for all h, h': the companion witnesses nothing.

Orthogonal branch states: if ⟨E_h'|E_h⟩ = δ_hh' on H_V, then G is the identity in every convention and V_A is diagonal; a cyclic product containing two different places vanishes, and one with all places equal is 1.
